request.spec:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each user can now switch columns of the people list on or off for their own screen. `bin/e2e` builds the app and runs the spec, and all 4 tests pass.

**What you'll see:** a "Columns" panel above the people list with a checkbox per column, `column-<id>`. Turning one off removes that column's value element (its `person-<id>` element) from every row. Totals, the header counters, the summary and the audit file are unchanged; nothing new is written to the audit file.

**Where the choice is kept:** in the browser's localStorage, keyed by the signed-in name. That keeps it to one user's screen and lets it survive reloading or switching sheets. It is not kept on the server, so it won't follow a user to another browser or device. If you want that, it would take a small per-user endpoint.

**Things worth knowing:**
- **An extra checkbox for `excess`.** The request doesn't list it, but the test switches `excess` off and expects its cell to go, so I added it.
- **Some columns keep their controls.** Hold, retired, aliases, patrons and the three statement figures share a cell with action buttons or inputs. For those, switching the column off removes the value but leaves the controls usable. For the plain columns (claimed, due-total, excess, overdue-count, overdue-total, backing, terms, contact), the whole cell and its table header are removed.

The new code is in `features/people/columns.ts` and `features/people/columnchooser.slot.tsx`. Each column's own slot file has a small change.
